rewrites.title: Genome-wide re-induction kinetics and priming
rewrites.description: Compare naive and previously stimulated cells after a rest period using nascent RNA assays (PRO-seq, TT-seq) at restimulation, quantifying faster or stronger induction genome-wide. This measures memory as primed responsiveness, not only persistent expression of canonical targets.

rewrites.title: Optogenetic test of AP-1 pulse sufficiency
rewrites.description: Drive AP-1 activity with an optogenetic or chemogenetic FOS/JUN system, with no upstream signal, using varied pulse patterns (single, repeated, sustained). Measure whether this alone leaves lasting accessibility and a primed transcriptional response, and map the dose–duration threshold for memory. This tests sufficiency and the dynamics required, rather than only necessity.

rewrites.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN after a transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., with injury, TNF, or growth factor), then profile chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding at multiple time points through washout and weeks later. Persistent AP-1 motif-containing open regions after signal withdrawal would indicate retained chromatin memory.

rewrites.title: Barcoded sister-cell lineage tracing through cell division
rewrites.description: Split sister cells after priming, then track them with lineage barcodes and paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq. Test whether AP-1 activity states and primed responses are inherited across divisions and decay at a rate predicted by AP-1 turnover. High sister-cell concordance would indicate heritable memory rather than ongoing signaling.

rewrites.title: Temporal ordering of AP-1 binding and accessibility after replication fork passage
rewrites.description: Use EdU-capture-coupled ATAC and CUT&RUN to determine, at minute-scale resolution after fork passage, whether AP-1 reoccupies its sites before accessibility returns or the reverse. Also image AP-1 retention on mitotic chromosomes. The temporal ordering identifies the physical carrier of the memory rather than just its correlates.

rewrites.title: DNA-based molecular recorder of AP-1 activity history
rewrites.description: Drive a prime-editing or recombinase-based recorder (e.g., ENGRAM or DNA Typewriter) from an AP-1-responsive promoter so each cell accumulates an ordered, cumulative record of its past AP-1 activity. Read the record and the current transcriptome from the same single cell. This separates integrated past AP-1 dose from present state without sorting or fixing cells at an arbitrarily chosen early timepoint.

rewrites.title: Washout time-course of AP-1 occupancy and chromatin state
rewrites.description: After a defined AP-1-inducing stimulus (e.g., TPA or serum), wash out and profile c-Fos/JunB/ATF3 occupancy (CUT&Tag) alongside ATAC-seq and H3K27ac at days 0 to 7. Memory is supported if enhancers stay open and retain AP-1 binding or priming marks after the TF signal has returned to baseline. Estimated cost is about $8k to $12k for a single cell line with 6 timepoints in duplicate.

rewrites.title: Surrogate bZIP domain swap
rewrites.description: In an AP-1-null or degron-depleted background, re-express a chimera of the AP-1 bZIP DNA-binding domain fused to a minimal heterologous activation domain, so the same motifs are bound and activated by a protein lacking AP-1's native cofactor and pioneer interactions. If the surrogate restores acute induction but not persistence, memory depends on AP-1 protein surfaces rather than motif occupancy alone.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degradation or dominant-negative block during priming versus maintenance
rewrites.description: Use degron tags (dTAG/AID) or inducible dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during priming or after memory has formed. Measure whether loss during priming prevents memory, and whether later loss erases it (accelerated transcriptional response and retained accessibility). This distinguishes AP-1 as an initiator from AP-1 as a maintainer.

rewrites.title: Mapping bZIP heterodimer partners at memory loci
rewrites.description: Use proximity labelling (TurboID or APEX) fused to JUN, FOS, ATF3 and JUNB, plus split-HaloTag complementation, to quantify which heterodimer partners occupy memory enhancers before, during and after priming. A persistent shift in partner composition, such as JUN-ATF3 replacing JUN-FOS, would indicate memory is encoded in a stable heterodimer switch rather than in AP-1 binding alone.

rewrites.title: Synthetic AP-1 tethering to endogenous enhancers
rewrites.description: Use dCas9 or a chemically inducible recruitment system to deposit AP-1 family members at defined endogenous enhancers for a controlled duration, release them, and then test whether the locus reactivates faster and more strongly upon a later real stimulus. This tests sufficiency, and dose and duration titration maps the minimum AP-1 exposure needed to install a persistent state.

rewrites.title: Sister-cell split with clonal barcodes and transplantation
rewrites.description: Barcode cells and let clones divide, then challenge one sister branch and use its response to predict the response of the untouched sister after the same priming history, as a function of intervening divisions. This gives a mitotic retention rate that separates heritable memory from noise. Transplanting primed cells into a naive microenvironment tests whether memory travels with the cell or with its context.

rewrites.title: Lineage-traced single-cell multiome of stimulus history
rewrites.description: Barcode cells, expose them to a transient stimulus, split them into sister lineages, and profile them by joint scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq after many divisions. Compare sister-cell concordance in AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression with unstimulated controls to measure heritable memory directly and determine its stability.

rewrites.title: Synthetic AP-1-only activation without the native stimulus
rewrites.description: Express a drug-inducible, AP-1-only synthetic activator (e.g., a constitutively active JUN/FOS fusion, pulsed and then removed) in naive cells and test whether it alone reproduces the primed accessibility and recall response of the natural stimulus. This sufficiency test separates AP-1 as a memory writer from other signaling arms such as NF-κB, MAPK or STAT that normally are co-activated.

rewrites.title: Optogenetic/chemogenetic AP-1 pulse timing with memory persistence readout
rewrites.description: Use light- or ligand-inducible FOS/JUN (or degron-controlled) to deliver defined pulses of AP-1 activity in AP-1-null cells, then measure whether enhancer accessibility and a reporter response persist after AP-1 is removed. Varying pulse duration, frequency, and delay before re-challenge defines the sufficiency, dose-dependence, and decay kinetics of memory.

rewrites.title: Cell-autonomy test by co-culture, transwell, and conditioned medium
rewrites.description: Prime one population, then co-culture it with naive, differently labeled cells, separate them with a transwell, or transfer conditioned medium, and measure whether the naive cells acquire faster re-induction. Repeat the experiment in an in vivo or transplant setting to check generalization. If the naive cells acquire the memory, it is not cell-intrinsic.

rewrites.title: Mitotic bookmarking and replication-coupled retention assay
rewrites.description: Combine CUT&Tag or live imaging of FOS/JUN on mitotic chromosomes with synchronization, EdU-based replication-timing and cell-cycle arrest experiments to test whether AP-1 stays on chromatin through mitosis. Comparing memory persistence in cells forced through division with that in arrested non-dividing cells shows whether memory depends on propagation across divisions or on a persistent chromatin state.

rewrites.title: Pulse-history and re-stimulation kinetics
rewrites.description: Vary the number, spacing and interval of AP-1-inducing pulses, then measure how fast and how strongly cells respond on re-stimulation. This shows whether AP-1 encodes input history in a way consistent with training-dependent memory, and the data can be fitted to a model.

rewrites.title: Stabilized AP-1 variant sufficiency and ensemble reactivation test
rewrites.description: Express a degradation-resistant or long-lived AP-1 isoform (e.g., a ΔFosB-like stabilized FOS) and test whether it extends the duration of induced chromatin and behavioral or functional changes beyond wild-type lifetimes. Pair this with activity-dependent ensemble tagging and optogenetic or chemogenetic reactivation to determine whether reactivating the tagged, AP-1-positive population is necessary and sufficient to recall the stored state.

rewrites.title: Mitotic live-imaging and CUT&RUN of AP-1
rewrites.description: Image endogenously HaloTag-labeled FOS/JUN with single-molecule tracking in mitotic versus interphase cells, and perform CUT&RUN on FACS-sorted mitotic cells. This tests whether AP-1 stays on chromatin through division, and whether its mitotic retention at specific enhancers predicts which sites reactivate fastest after mitosis.
